newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower after crude slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower after crude slide.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to lower again Friday in lackluster activity, with cratering crude and natgas markets still undermining sentiment, industry sources said.
"The crude selloff could be the death knell for resid. Winter is just about over," said one cash trader, noting buyers headed for the sidelines late this week as crude and gas crumbled.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was steady to down slightly to about $17.50 a barrel, with March paper also modestly lower at about $17, traders said.
Traders said talk that some East Coast utilities switched to gas recently kept low sulphur sentiment bearish, but NYH 0.3 percent high pour was little changed in the $20.25-50 area.
U.S. Gulf refinery problems continued to weigh on high sulphur grades.
NYH 2.2 percent was down slightly to $15.75 area, while U.S. Gulf three percent tumbled another 50 cents or so to about $13.
USG one percent slipped 20 cents to $16.25 though some thought the number was in the $15s.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate weekend gas prices slipped 10 cents into the $2.90/mmBtu area. NYH one percent resid fell to a $2.78/mmBtu equivalent.
